objectives: Students will review and demonstrate their understanding of area, quadrilateral properties, polyhedra, nets, and surface area. They will choose appropriate formulas and strategies, identify corresponding bases and perpendicular heights, decompose figures, and account for every face of a solid. Students will explain their reasoning, correct errors, and use appropriate units as they prepare for Friday's test.
agenda:
Monday, October 19: Area and Quadrilateral Review
Review quadrilateral classifications and parallelogram side and angle relationships. Practice finding the areas of rectangles, parallelograms, and triangles using corresponding bases and perpendicular heights. Find polygon areas by decomposing, rearranging, or subtracting simpler shapes.

Tuesday, October 20: Polyhedra, Nets, and Surface Area Review
Identify prisms and pyramids and count their faces, edges, and vertices. Match solids to nets and calculate surface area by adding the areas of all faces, including hidden faces. Check that each face is counted exactly once.

Wednesday, October 21: Mixed Review and Test Preparation
Complete mixed practice covering the topics learned so far. Compare strategies, correct mistakes, and ask questions. Review the difference between surface area and volume, including square units versus cubic units. Identify which skills you need to practice before Friday's test.
Thursday, October 22: Field Trip to Fenway Park

Friday, October 23: Test – Area, Surface Area, and Geometry
Demonstrate your understanding of the topics reviewed this week. Work independently, show your calculations and reasoning, label answers with the correct units, and check your work.
homework: Complete assigned DeltaMath review practice. Study your class notes and corrected review problems for Friday's test, focusing on skills you still find challenging. Bring your notebook, paper, and a sharpened pencil to every class.
languageObjectives: Students will explain and justify area strategies using the terms base, perpendicular height, decompose, and square units.
Students will describe quadrilateral properties and polyhedra using precise vocabulary, including parallel, congruent, supplementary, face, edge, vertex, prism, pyramid, and net.
Students will compare solutions, explain corrections, and distinguish surface area from volume using appropriate mathematical terms and units.

objectives: By the end of the week, students will identify faces, edges, and vertices of polyhedra; connect solids to their nets; and calculate the surface area of prisms and pyramids by adding the areas of all faces. Students will explain their calculations and label answers in square units. If time allows, students will distinguish surface area from volume.
agenda: Monday, October 12: No School – Indigenous Peoples' Day

Tuesday, October 13: Lesson 13 Review and Lesson 14 – Nets and Surface Area
Review faces, edges, and vertices of prisms and pyramids. Match solids to their nets and explain how each face of a solid appears in its net.

Wednesday, October 14: Continue Lesson 14 – Nets and Surface Area
Use nets to organize surface-area calculations. Find the area of each face, include every face exactly once, and add the areas. Compare your method with a partner and label your answer in square units.

Thursday, October 15: Lesson 15 – More Nets, More Surface Area
Find the surface areas of prisms and pyramids using nets and labeled dimensions. Apply rectangle and triangle area formulas, identify corresponding bases and perpendicular heights, and justify your calculations.

Friday, October 16: Surface Area Practice and Review
Practice using nets, check for missing or double-counted faces, and explain your reasoning. If ready: Lesson 16 – Distinguishing Between Surface Area and Volume (Optional). Compare covering the outside of a solid with the space it occupies, using square units for surface area and cubic units for volume.
homework: Complete assigned DeltaMath practice. Review rectangle and triangle area formulas and use your class notes to practice finding surface area from a net. Bring your notebook, paper, and a sharpened pencil to every class.
languageObjectives: Students will describe polyhedra and their nets using the terms face, edge, vertex, prism, and pyramid.
Students will explain and compare surface-area strategies, stating how each face was counted and why the total is measured in square units.

If ready for the optional extension, students will explain the difference between surface area and volume using the phrases covering the outside and occupying space, and the terms square units and cubic units.

objectives: By the end of the week, students will describe surface area as the total area of all the faces of a polyhedron, identify faces, edges, and vertices, and connect three-dimensional solids to their two-dimensional nets. Students will calculate surface area by adding the areas of all faces and label answers in square units. As an optional extension, students will distinguish surface area from volume.
agenda:
Day 1 – Monday: Lesson 12 – What Is Surface Area?
Explore how much material is needed to cover the outside of a solid. Find surface area by adding the areas of every face, including faces hidden from view, and express the total in square units.

Day 2 – Tuesday: Lesson 13 – Polyhedra
Identify and count faces, edges, and vertices. Describe and compare prisms and pyramids using the shapes of their faces and the way those faces meet.

Day 3 – Wednesday: Lesson 14 – Nets and Surface Area
Match nets to the solids they form. Use a net to organize the areas of all faces and calculate the surface area, counting each face exactly once.

Day 4 – Thursday: Lesson 15 – More Nets, More Surface Area
Use nets and labeled dimensions to find the surface areas of prisms and pyramids. Apply rectangle and triangle area formulas, choose corresponding bases and perpendicular heights, and explain your calculations.

Day 5 – Friday: Surface Area Review and Lesson 16 – Distinguishing Between Surface Area and Volume (Optional)
Review finding surface area with nets and compare solution strategies. As an optional extension, distinguish the area covering a solid from the space it occupies and explain when to use square units or cubic units.
homework: Complete assigned DeltaMath practice. Review rectangle and triangle area formulas, the parts of polyhedra, and how nets help organize surface-area calculations. Bring your notebook, paper, and a sharpened pencil to class every day.
languageObjectives: Students will describe and compare solids using the terms polyhedron, face, edge, vertex, prism, and pyramid.
Students will explain how a net represents a solid and justify surface-area calculations using the terms face area, total area, and square units.
As an optional extension, students will compare surface area and volume using the phrases covering the outside and occupying space, and distinguish square units from cubic units.

objectives: By the end of the week, students will explain how triangle area relates to parallelogram area, identify a base and its corresponding perpendicular height, use A = (b × h) ÷ 2 to find triangle areas, and find polygon areas by decomposing them into simpler shapes. Students will explain their reasoning and label areas in square units.
agenda:
Day 1 – Monday: Lesson 7 – From Parallelograms to Triangles
Split a parallelogram along a diagonal into two congruent triangles. Use diagrams to explain why each triangle has half the area of the parallelogram.

Day 2 – Tuesday: Lesson 8 – Area of Triangles
Find triangle areas by composing two congruent copies into a parallelogram or by decomposing shapes with known areas. Compare strategies with a partner and explain your reasoning.

Day 3 – Wednesday: Lesson 9 – Formula for the Area of a Triangle
Explain the one-half factor in A = (b × h) ÷ 2. Use the formula to calculate triangle areas and label answers in square units.

Day 4 – Thursday: Lesson 10 – Bases and Heights of Triangles
Choose a base and identify or draw its corresponding perpendicular height. Find heights inside or outside a triangle, extending the base when needed, and distinguish height from a slanted side length.

Day 5 – Friday: Lesson 11 – Polygons
Find polygon areas by decomposing figures into non-overlapping triangles, rectangles, or parallelograms and adding their areas. Compare different decompositions and justify why they give the same total area.
homework: Complete assigned DeltaMath practice. Review your notes on triangle area, bases and heights, and polygon decomposition. Bring your notebook, paper, and a sharpened pencil to class every day.
languageObjectives: Students will explain the relationship between triangle and parallelogram areas using the terms congruent, one-half, base, and height.
Students will describe how a height is perpendicular to its corresponding base or the line containing that base.
Students will compare and justify polygon area strategies using the terms decompose, non-overlapping, polygon, and square units.

objectives: By the end of the week, students will calculate the area of parallelograms, use the properties of parallelograms to find missing side and angle measures, and classify different types of quadrilaterals.
agenda:
Day 1 – Monday: Area of Parallelograms
Identify a base and its corresponding perpendicular height, then use A = b × h to find the area of a parallelogram. Explain how cutting and rearranging a parallelogram forms a rectangle with the same area.

Day 2 – Tuesday: Parallelogram Properties and Quadrilaterals
Use the facts that opposite sides are parallel and congruent, opposite angles are congruent, and consecutive angles are supplementary to find missing side and angle measures. Classify and label parallelograms, rectangles, rhombuses, squares, trapezoids, and other quadrilaterals.

Day 3 – Wednesday: Applying Parallelogram Relationships
Solve problems involving area, missing bases or heights, missing side lengths, and missing angle measures. Justify each answer using a parallelogram property.

Day 4 – Thursday: Quiz Review
Complete mixed practice on parallelogram area, angle relationships, side relationships, and quadrilateral classification. Ask questions and correct misunderstandings before the quiz.

Day 5 – Friday: Quiz
Demonstrate your understanding of parallelogram area and properties and the classification of quadrilaterals.
homework: Complete assigned DeltaMath or review practice. Bring your notebook, paper, and a sharpened pencil to class every day. Study Thursday's review for Friday's quiz.
languageObjectives: Students will explain how a base and its corresponding perpendicular height determine the area of a parallelogram.
Students will justify missing measures and classifications using the terms opposite, consecutive, parallel, congruent, supplementary, and quadrilateral.

objectives: By the end of the week, students will explain the meaning of area and use tiling, decomposing, rearranging, enclosing, and subtracting to find and compare the areas of two-dimensional figures.
agenda:
Day 1 – Monday: Check Your Readiness
Show what you already know about area, rectangles, parallel and perpendicular lines, and geometric figures. Explain your reasoning whenever possible.

Day 2 – Tuesday: Reasoning to Find Area
Tiling the Plane: Compare geometric patterns and explain how shapes cover a region without gaps or overlaps.
Finding Area by Decomposing and Rearranging: Find area by composing smaller shapes, decomposing figures, and rearranging pieces into familiar shapes.

Day 3 – Wednesday: MAP Test English
Complete the MAP English assessment carefully and give your best effort.

Day 4 – Thursday: MAP Test Math
Complete the MAP Mathematics assessment carefully, use scratch paper, and show perseverance.

Day 5 – Friday: Reasoning to Find Area
Use different strategies to find the area of polygons, compare strategies, explain your reasoning, and label answers with square units.
homework: Complete any assigned DeltaMath practice. Bring your notebook, paper, and a sharpened pencil to class every day.
languageObjectives: Students will explain that area is the amount of the plane covered by a two-dimensional region.
Students will compare and explain area strategies using the terms tile, compose, decompose, rearrange, and square units.

objectives: By the end of the week, students will build our classroom community, learn the routines and materials needed for math class, set up DeltaMath, and demonstrate what they remember from Grade 5 math.
agenda: Tuesday: Welcome to 6th Grade Math; make name tents; meet our class; review daily materials; receive an available take-home IM book; and begin the Grade 5 math diagnostic.
Wednesday: Complete the Grade 5 math diagnostic and register for DeltaMath.
Thursday: Practice our classroom routines and begin our first math lesson.
Friday: Continue the math lesson, share strategies, and reflect on our first week.
Name-Tent Directions: Fold an 8.5 × 11-inch sheet into thirds so it stands. Write your name large, dark, and easy to read. At the bottom, add one sport or activity you enjoy.
Daily Materials: Bring a notebook, paper, and a pencil to every class.
homework: Bring your notebook, paper, and a pencil every day. Keep your assigned math book at home for review.
languageObjectives: Students will introduce themselves and share one sport or activity they enjoy.
Students will explain their mathematical thinking and describe the strategies they use.
